title: Pacific Life's $58.3 Million IUL Settlement (TEST RENDER)
description: IUL policyholders were promised market-tied growth with a guaranteed floor — but a $58.3M settlement against Pacific Life, finalized May 2026, shows how illustrated projections can diverge from what a policy actually pays out.
sourceCitation: TEST RENDER — fictional documents, not real evidence. Not financial advice. Sourcing pending (Stage 2 / CourtListener).

scenes.captionText: They paid millions. Here's the document that proves it.
scenes.narrationText: This settlement document is real. And it's not the only one.

scenes.captionText: $XX.X million. One sentence buried in the filing.
scenes.narrationText: Right here — the exact number. This is what a policyholder actually recovered, and it's written in plain language most people never read.

scenes.captionText: But the real question isn't the settlement. It's how the gap happened.
scenes.narrationText: The settlement is the outcome. This is the input — the actual illustration page handed to policyholders at the point of sale.

scenes.captionText: This one assumption drove the entire gap.
scenes.narrationText: This line — the assumed crediting rate — is the number that made the projection look nothing like reality. Change this one input, and the whole illustration falls apart.

scenes.captionText: Check your own illustration for this same line.
scenes.narrationText: If you hold a policy like this, pull your original illustration and find this same assumption. It's usually on the first page of numbers.
